name: Ertapenem
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ertapenem is eliminated mainly by the kidneys (about 80% in urine, half as unchanged drug). The US label keeps 1 g once daily down to a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 31 mL/min/1.73 m2 and gives 500 mg once daily at 30 or less, including end-stage kidney disease. On hemodialysis, a 150 mg supplement follows the session only if the daily dose was given within 6 hours before it.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl in mL/min/1.73 m2 (Cockcroft–Gault formula quoted); cut-off 30.

bands.recommendation: No dose change (label: CrCl above 30 mL/min/1.73 m2): 1 g once daily.
No dose change (label: CrCl above 30 mL/min/1.73 m2): 1 g once daily.
CrCl 30 or less: 500 mg once daily (label).
500 mg once daily, including end-stage kidney disease (CrCl 10 or less) (label).

hd: 500 mg once daily. If the dose is given within 6 hours before hemodialysis, give 150 mg after the session; if given at least 6 hours before, no supplement (label). Literature option (not label): thrice-weekly after each session, 500 mg, 500 mg and 500 mg, or 1 g, 1 g and 1 g (evidence too limited to prefer one) (Tsai 2025). These regimens are not weight-adjusted and come mostly from small pharmacokinetic studies; confirm the actual last and next session before each dose. See the site guide Antibiotic Stewardship in Hemodialysis (/guides/antibiotic-stewardship-dialysis.html).
pd: No data in peritoneal dialysis (label). ISPD 2022 gives no intraperitoneal ertapenem dose. Specialist input.
crrt: No hemofiltration data in label. Li 2020 (Table 3): CVVHD dialysate 1–3 L/h, or CVVHDF combined flow 36–51 mL/kg/h: 500 mg every 24 hours, 750 mg every 24 hours, 500 mg every 12 hours or 1,000 mg every 24 hours.
dialyzable: Partly: about 30% of a 1 g dose was recovered in dialysate during a 4-hour hemodialysis started right after the dose (label). Highly protein bound (85% to 95%).
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures and other CNS effects, mainly with CNS disorders or reduced kidney function (label); valproate levels if coadministered.

pediatric.approved_ages: 3 months to 17 years; not recommended under 3 months (no data) or for meningitis (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: 3 months to 12 years: 15 mg/kg twice daily (maximum 1 g/day); 13 years and older: 1 g once daily (label).

renal.recommendation: No data in pediatric patients with kidney impairment or on hemodialysis (label). Specialist input.
